description: Open Source framework for voice agents, multimodal apps, and realtime AI. Maintained by Daily and the community.

latest_release.name: v1.15.0
latest_release.body:
### Added

- Added a `custom_configuration` field to `NvidiaTTSService.Settings`, which forwards model-specific key/value parameters to NVIDIA TTS — Magpie's `flush`, `chunk_len_threshold` and `max_chunk_threshold` streaming controls, or Chatterbox's `exaggeration_factor`.
  (PR [#5580](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/pull/5580))

- Added `ClassifierUserTurnStopStrategy` and `ClassifierUserTurnStrategies`, which let a classifier, such as `JevClassifier`, decide whether the user's turn is complete. They're an alternative to `FilterIncompleteUserTurnStrategies` for an LLM that doesn't follow the turn-completion markers well. At every pause with new words, the classifier judges the turn so far from the user's words and the bot's last line: `complete` ends the turn, and `short` and `long` keep it open for a few seconds unless the user continues. `ClassifierUserTurnStrategies` adds the classifier to the default stop strategies (smart turn), and the turn ends once both have decided; for the classifier alone, pass `UserTurnStrategies(stop=[ClassifierUserTurnStopStrategy(...)])`.

    ```python
    user_params = LLMUserAggregatorParams(
        user_turn_strategies=ClassifierUserTurnStrategies(
            classifier=JevClassifier(api_key=os.getenv("TYPESAFE_API_KEY")),
            context=context,
        ),
    )
    ```
  (PR [#5870](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/pull/5870))

- Added `number_pronunciation_language` to `SmallestTTSService` settings, which reads numerals, currency, times and dates in a language of its own, independent of the synthesis language.
  (PR [#5936](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/pull/5936))

- Added `text_matches` to scripted eval expectations: one or more regular expressions the event's text must each match, such as a format a reply must open with. A miss fails the expectation with the new `text_unmatched` failure kind.
  (PR [#5991](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/pull/5991))

- `LLMWithBackend(predictive_delegation=PredictiveDelegation(classifier))` is an optimization that can speed up responses that need backend involvement. It uses a fast yes/no classifier (such as `JevClassifier`) to determine, after each user request, whether it needs to wait for a frontend inference or can go ahead and trigger an early backend delegation. The cost is money, not time: the classifier runs in parallel with the frontend, but on every turn, and an early delegation abandons a frontend request already under way. Only text frontends are supported, and only request strategies that have `BackendRequestStrategy.delegate_needs_arguments` set to `False` (like `TranscriptBackendRequestStrategy`).
  (PR [#6174](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/pull/6174))

- Added `AICTytoObserver`, which scores the quality of the user's audio with the ai-coustics Tyto model after every 5 seconds of received audio. Each result fires the `on_analysis_result` event with the risk score and per-degradation scores. At the end of the call, `on_call_summary` receives the mean, p95, and max scores, the degraded fraction, and the dominant degradation dimension. Pass the transport's `AICFilter` as `audio_filter` to score the audio before enhancement.
  (PR [#6181](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/pull/6181))

- `AWSBedrockLLMService` now emits the reasoning a model returns in `reasoningContent` (Claude with extended thinking, Nova 2 with reasoning enabled) as `LLMThoughtStartFrame` / `LLMThoughtTextFrame` / `LLMThoughtEndFrame`. Signed reasoning, such as Claude's, is kept in the context and passed back to the model on later turns, so Claude keeps its reasoning across tool calls.
  (PR [#6229](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/pull/6229))

- `TavusTransport` and `TavusVideoService` now set the Tavus replica's facial emotion from the delivery the bot speaks in, when expressive conversation is enabled (`PipelineParams(enable_expressive_conversation=True)`). They convert each `TTSTextFrame.delivery` to a `TavusEmotion` a

Add WordTTSService support for aws PollyTTSService
TranscriptionFrame queued behind the frame that starts a user turn is dropped by that turn's own interruption
AnthropicLLMService: after a tool or system prompt change, every later request fails with a 400 on accounts with preserved thinking enforced
Interruption loses played TTS text from assistant context (InterruptionFrame overtakes released TTSTextFrames + transport queue drop) — bot repeats itself
Proposal: graceful interruption release for TTS/output transports
Option to Initiate Outbound Whatsapp Business Call
Support for combined STT + LLM with gpt4o-audio-preview

detail.readme: [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/pipecat-ai)](https://pypi.org/project/pipecat-ai) ![Tests](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/actions/workflows/tests.yaml/badge.svg) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/pipecat-ai/pipecat/graph/badge.svg?token=LNVUIVO4Y9)](https://codecov.io/gh/pipecat-ai/pipecat) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Documentation-blue)](https://docs.pipecat.ai) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1239284677165056021)](https://discord.gg/pipecat) [![Ask DeepWiki](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ask-DeepWiki-blue)](https://deepwiki.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat) # 🎙️ Pipecat: Real-Time Voice & Multimodal AI Agents **Pipecat** is an open-source Python framework for building real-time voice and multimodal conversational agents. Build a single voice agent or a full multi-agent system where specialists hand off, fan out in parallel, and coordinate over a shared bus, locally or distributed across processes and machines. Orchestrate audio and video, AI services, transports, and conversation pipelines effortlessly, so you can focus on what makes your agents unique. > Want to dive right in? Run `pipecat init quickstart` or follow the [quickstart guide](https://docs.pipecat.ai/getting-started/quickstart). ## 🚀 What you can build - **Voice Assistants** – natural, streaming conversations with AI - **Multi-Agent Systems** – specialists that hand off, fan out in parallel, or run as sidecars over a shared bus - **AI Companions** – coaches, meeting assistants, characters - **Multimodal Interfaces** – voice, video, images, and more - **Interactive Storytelling** – creative tools with generative media - **Business Agents** – customer intake, support bots, guided flows - **Complex Dialog Systems** – design logic with structured conversations ## 🧠 Why Pipecat? - **Voice-first**: Integrates speech recognition, text-to-speech, and conversation handling - **Pluggable**: Supports many AI services and tools - **Composable Pipelines**: Build complex behavior from modular components - **Multi-Agent Ready**: Each pipeline is an agent. Compose them with handoff, parallel fan-out, sidecar workers, or distributed deployments - **Real-Time**: Ultra-low latency interaction with different transports (e.g. WebSockets or WebRTC) ## 🌐 Pipecat ecosystem ### 📱 Client SDKs Building client applications? You can connect to Pipecat from any platform using our official SDKs: JavaScript | React | React Native | Swift | Kotlin | C++ | ESP32 ### 🧭 Structured conversations Need predefined or dynamic conversation paths with state management? [Pipecat Flows](https://docs.pipecat.ai/guides/features/pipecat-flows) is built into Pipecat. Browse the [examples](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/tree/main/examples/flows) to see it in action. ### 🪄 Beautiful UIs Want to build beautiful and engaging experiences? Check out [Pipecat UI](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat-ui), a shadcn registry of components for building voice AI applications. Browse the [documentation](https://ui.pipecat.ai/) for component previews and installation guides. ### 🛠️ Create and deploy projects The [Pipecat CLI](https://docs.pipecat.ai/api-reference/cli/overview) ships with `pipecat-ai` — install it with `uv tool install "pipecat-ai[cli]"`. Run `pipecat init` to start a project: it sets you up so an AI coding assistant (Claude Code, Codex) builds it for you, and can scaffold a runnable bot in under a minute. Then use the CLI to monitor and deploy your agent to production. ### 🔍 Debugging Looking for help debugging your pipeline and processors? Check out [Whisker](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/whisker), a real-time Pipecat debugger. ### 🖥️ Terminal Love terminal applications? Check out [Tail](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/tail), a terminal dashboard for Pipecat. ### 🤖 Claude Code skills Use [Pipecat Skills](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/skills) with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) to scaffold projects, deploy to Pipecat Cloud, and more. Install the marketplace with: ``` claude plugin marketplace add pipecat-ai/skills ``` and install any of the available plugins. ### 🧩 Community integrations Build and share your own Pipecat service integrations! Browse existing [community integrations](https://docs.pipecat.ai/api-reference/server/services/supported-services) or check out our [guide](COMMUNITY_INTEGRATIONS.md) to create your own. ### 📺️ Pipecat TV channel Catch new features, interviews, and how-tos on our [Pipecat TV](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLzU2zoMTQIHjqC3v4q2XVSR3hGSzwKFwH) channel. ## 🎬 See it in action | Example | What it shows | | ------- | ------------- | | 📞 [**Phone agent**](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat-examples#telephony--voice-calls) | Answers incoming calls and places outbound calls. Examples for [Twilio](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat-examples/tree/main/twilio-chatbot), [Telnyx](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat-examples/tree/main/telnyx-chatbot), [Plivo](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat-examples/tree/main/plivo-chatbot), [Exotel](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat-examples/tree/main/exotel-chatbot), [Vonage](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat-examples/tree/main/vonage-audio-bot), [Genesys](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat-examples/tree/main/genesys-chatbot) and [Daily PSTN and SIP](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat-examples/tree/main/phone-chatbot). | | 🧠 [**Voice LLM with a tool-calling backend**](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/tree/main/examples/multi-worker/llm-with-backend) | `LLMWithBackend` pairs a fast voice model with a slower backend model that runs the tools, and the voice keeps talking while the backend works. | | 🎭 [**Expressive conversation**](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/tree/main/examples/expressive-conversation) | The LLM writes emotion and sound tags such as laughter into its replies, and the TTS performs them. →](https://docs.pipecat.ai/api-reference/server/services/supported-services) | 📚 [View full services documentation →](https://docs.pipecat.ai/api-reference/server/services/supported-services) ## ⚡ Getting started Run Pipecat on your local machine, then move your agent processes to the cloud when you're ready. Either way, you'll need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) — install it first: ```bash curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh ``` ### Start a new project with the CLI The quickest path: install the Pipecat CLI and scaffold a new phone or web/mobile bot interactively. ```bash uv tool install "pipecat-ai[cli]" pipecat init ``` Follow the [quickstart guide](https://docs.pipecat.ai/getting-started/quickstart) to get your very first bot running, or dive a little deeper into [bootstrapping a project](https://docs.pipecat.ai/pipecat/get-started/build-your-next-bot). ### Add to an existing project ```bash uv add pipecat-ai ``` To keep things lightweight, only the core framework is included by default. Add extras for the third-party AI services you use: ```bash uv add "pipecat-ai[option,...]" ``` > **Using pip?** `pip install pipecat-ai` and `pip install "pipecat-ai[option,...]"` work too. Pipecat runs on Python 3.11 through 3.14. Python 3.15 is not supported yet, because `onnxruntime` publishes no wheels for it. Pin your project to a supported version, for example with `uv python pin 3.14`. From here, the code examples below are the best way to learn — agents you can run, read, and adapt. ## 🧪 Code examples - [Focused examples](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/tree/main/examples) — small agents that each illustrate one or two specific services or concepts - [Example apps](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat-examples) — complete applications you can use as starting points for development ## 🛠️ Developing Pipecat ### Prerequisites **Minimum Python Version:** 3.11 **Recommended Python Version:** >= 3.12 ### Setup steps 1. Clone the repository and navigate to it: ```bash git clone https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat.git cd pipecat ``` 2. Install development and testing dependencies: ```bash uv sync --group dev --all-extras \ --no-extra gstreamer \ --no-extra local ``` 3. Install the git pre-commit hooks: ```bash uv run pre-commit install ``` > **Note**: Some extras (local, gstreamer) require system dependencies. See documentation if you encounter build errors. ### Claude Code skills Install development workflow skills for contributing to Pipecat with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code): ``` claude plugin marketplace add pipecat-ai/pipecat claude plugin install pipecat-dev@pipecat-dev-skills ``` ### Running tests To run all tests, from the root directory: ```bash uv run pytest ``` Tests run in parallel, one worker per CPU core. Pass `-n 0` to run them in a single process. Run a specific test suite: ```bash uv run pytest tests/test_name.py ``` ## 🤝 Contributing We welcome contributions from the community!
